solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Expect chemical company head back to worker

indicators.note: the company and head are set behind, backing on to, the worker

parts.note: a worker is a type of ant, the classic crossword insect
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a big British chemical company
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A chemical firm's boss is posted back to the shop floor, as might be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the company boss, but it is just a word for the top of the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to look forward to it as likely, a direct synonym of expect.

clue.text: Commander turned up carrying explosives, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the word Commander carries the letters within itself

explanation.surface: An officer gets out of the trench carrying explosive charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' hides OMMA in commANDer's middle; 'turned up' then reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition, shortened to its slang form, covers shells and charges, of which explosives are one example.

clue.text: Reach end of flight and feel sad

parts.note: to feel something is to touch it
feeling down means feeling sad

explanation.surface: A passenger lands at the end of a journey and feels low.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's touchdown is the moment its wheels meet the runway when the flight ends.

clue.text: Piece of music unknown in a dance arrangement

indicators.note: the unknown letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
an arrangement of a dance reorders its letters

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A musical piece has an unknown section in a dance arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' turns A DANCE into CADENA, and 'in' puts Z between the N and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is a showy solo passage within a concerto, so a section or piece of music.

clue.text: Component that is needed in computer upgrade at last

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is must be put inside the computer abbreviation

parts.note: PC stands for personal computer
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: only the final letter of upgrade is taken

explanation.surface: A part that is required when a computer is finally upgraded.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of a machine or set is one of its parts, as a component is.

clue.text: Staff right upset, given meal with no starter

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the letters are turned over, bottom to top
the meal word loses its first letter, its starter

parts.note: a luncheon is a formal midday meal

explanation.surface: Staff are rightly upset when given a meal without a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' and 'starter' read as restaurant talk; staff here is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short club carried by police, a kind of staff or cudgel.

clue.text: Maybe puts icing on jam rolls

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to be in a jam or in a spot is to be in trouble

explanation.surface: A baker puts icing on jam rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam rolls' look like cakes; jam is a fix and rolls is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing a cake finishes its upper surface, so the baker crowns or caps it, one example of the verb.

clue.text: Round sort of biscuit kept for later?

parts.note: the letter O is round
a Nice biscuit is a sugar-topped coconut biscuit popular in Britain

explanation.surface: A round biscuit set aside to eat later.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nice biscuit (said like the French city) is a common British coconut biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on ice are suspended, saved for a future time, an idiom; the question mark flags the idiom.

clue.text: Tracey Ullman hit performed by female group?

parts.note: a song performed has been sung
lasses are girls, a group of females

explanation.surface: A Tracey Ullman single is covered by a girl band.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Ullman is an English comic actor who had pop hits in 1983-84.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullman's 1984 single, one of her chart hits, carried this title, the word for tinted eyewear.

clue.text: Singer turns up unusual score

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: ten-nil is a rare scoreline in a football match

explanation.surface: A vocalist arrives with an unusual musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' wants to be sheet music; it is a match result, and 'unusual' is part of the definition of it, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small finch known for its song, and birds are singers in crosswords.

clue.text: French individual engaged by government department makes a pile

indicators.note: one piece is taken on, held, inside the other

parts.note: the MoD is Britain's Ministry of Defence
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A Frenchman hired by Whitehall gets rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a pile' suggests getting rich; pile here is a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of earth or stones, a pile, is a hillock or mound.

clue.text: Russell's early letters included in publication showing scholarship

indicators.note: the letters are put inside the publication word

parts.note: an edition is one issue or printing of a publication

indicators.note: the first two letters of the name are taken

explanation.surface: An edition of Bertrand Russell's early letters displays scholarship.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep learning, a synonym of scholarship in its sense of learnedness.

clue.text: Coppers making a difference

definitions.meaning: copper coins are small loose cash in a pocket
an alteration or variation from before

explanation.surface: Police officers make a difference to the community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police; it is the coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Small coins are loose cash, and an alteration from what was is also this word; two senses.

clue.text: For example, after setback, a Liberal joins Tory set

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: the abbreviation is set back, reversed, and placed after

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: After a setback, a Liberal joins the Tory set, for example in a coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a group of people; it means to harden.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquids congeal when they solidify or thicken, as jelly sets.

clue.text: Clipped writing style copy editor banned

indicators.note: clipped means the word is cut short at its end

parts.note: prose is ordinary written style, not verse
to crib is to copy another's work

explanation.surface: An editor bans a terse writing style that copies others.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proscribed is forbidden or outlawed, a synonym of banned.

clue.text: Wine from heart of Loire knocked back with German's approval

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, and here the letters go backwards
the middle letters of the word, without its ends

parts.note: ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A wine from the heart of the Loire is drunk, to German approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' sounds like drinking; it reverses OIR to RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Spanish region of the same name.

clue.text: Upsets, as pot is found in public school

indicators.note: the pot word is located inside the other pieces

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
an urn is a large pot or vase

explanation.surface: Drugs found at a public school cause upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' looks like cannabis; it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn a ruling or a boat is to upset it, reversing or capsizing it.

clue.text: During trip, kid is infuriating

indicators.note: something happening during the trip sits inside it

parts.note: an outing is a short trip
to kid or rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A child on a school trip is infuriating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child; here it is the verb tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Outraging someone makes them furious, a near synonym of infuriating.

clue.text: Introduction taped by fantastic star performer

indicators.note: the introduction is enclosed, as if taped round, by the other letters
fantastic means wild or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Part I is the opening section of a book, its introduction

explanation.surface: A fantastic star records the introduction to a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduction' looks like a mere opening to the surface; it is the heading of a book's first section, Part I, and 'fantastic' scrambles the star around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapper or MC delivers rhymed lyrics over beats, one example of a performer.

clue.text: Keep celebrating, allowed to enter only one club?

indicators.note: the allowed word goes into the other phrase

parts.note: to sing on is to keep going with a celebratory song
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Partygoers keep celebrating after being allowed into the one club.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a lone card in one suit is a singleton; club is the suit, not a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: In a hand of cards, holding a single card of a suit, such as a lone club, is this.

clue.text: Lean on fighter

parts.note: a ship that leans to one side is said to list
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lean on a fighter to get the result you want.
explanation.walkthrough: Sonny Liston was a world heavyweight boxing champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Liston was a heavyweight boxer, an example of a fighter by name.

clue.text: Male has removed middle bit from fruit tree

indicators.note: the central letter of the fruit word is taken away

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: A man cuts the middle out of the fruit from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit tree' reads as one item; the definition is just 'tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a tree, source of syrup and of Canada's leaf emblem.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink — bar unfortunately runs out early

parts.note: a Mars bar is a chocolate bar

indicators.note: the word stops short, losing its last letter

parts.note: alas means unfortunately

explanation.surface: Sadly, the bar runs out of drink early in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub; it is a Mars, a well-known British chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily, a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Here's coffee and caviare, mate announced

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word given is how the letters sound

parts.note: caviare is fish roe, and buster is a casual address for a mate or chap

explanation.surface: A waiter announces coffee and caviare to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'roe buster' sounds like the coffee's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Robusta is one of the two main species of coffee bean grown commercially.

clue.text: Plant beginning to revive in economic upturn

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the boom word

parts.note: a boom is a period of fast economic growth

indicators.note: only the opening letter of revive is taken

explanation.surface: A plant begins to revive in an economic recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory reviving in good times; it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Broom is a yellow-flowered shrub, a plant of heaths and hillsides.

clue.text: Chap changed gear, taking minor road

indicators.note: changed means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RD is the short form of road

explanation.surface: A man changes gear while turning onto a minor road.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerard is a man's given name, and chap stands for any man in crosswords.

clue.text: Boarded, taking journey northwards

parts.note: to go is to make a journey
northwards is to the north, and N abbreviates north

explanation.surface: A passenger gets on board for a trip up north.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on a bus or train is boarding it; past tense matches.

clue.text: After party, empty room where several people can sleep

indicators.note: the room piece follows after the party piece

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: emptied of its insides, the word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: After a party, a room is cleared for guests to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormitory, shortened, is a shared room with beds for many sleepers.

clue.text: Igloo's constructed in part for scientist

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the part word

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece

indicators.note: constructed means built up anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An igloo is built partly for a polar scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Igloo's' supplies a letter: 'constructed' makes OLOGIS from IGLOOS, set 'in' BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A biologist studies living things, one kind of scientist.

clue.text: Foreign friend recalled long film, say, forgetting odd extracts

indicators.note: called back, so the letters are read in reverse
the odd letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A friend from abroad recalls a long film, but forgets odd scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting odd extracts' keeps OGIMA, the even letters, which 'recalled' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used in English for a foreign pal.

clue.text: Panto character in Mother Goose finale

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

indicators.note: the last letter of Goose is taken

explanation.surface: A pantomime figure takes part in the finale of Mother Goose.
explanation.walkthrough: The pantomime dame, a man in drag, is a British Christmas-show stock role, and Mother Goose is a panto.
explanation.definitionFit: The dame is the comic older woman played by a man in British pantomime.

clue.text: Perhaps a male couple discussed as part of meeting?

indicators.note: talked about, so it is the spoken sound that counts

parts.note: male is one example of a gender, and a couple are an item

explanation.surface: A gay couple is the subject of discussion at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'a gender' and 'agenda' sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Each topic listed for discussion at a meeting is one of its points, a part of the business.
